vars.label: Median land surface temperature, summer nights (ECOSTRESS, °C)
vars.ref: NASA ECOSTRESS ECO_L2T_LSTE version 2 (70 m), 295 night granules of June to September 2024-2026 between 21:00 and 06:00, read from the LP DAAC; the median of each 60 m cell's clear views (https://doi.org/10.5067/ECOSTRESS/ECO_L2T_LSTE.002)
vars.definition: The median of the land's surface temperature at night over the area: half the land is warmer. Land surface temperature is the radiative temperature of the ground, roofs, pavement and tree canopy, measured by the satellite's thermal sensor; it is not the air temperature. At night, pavement, roofs and walls give back the heat they stored during the day, so built land stays warmer than fields and forest: this is what keeps a city from cooling down. ECOSTRESS flies on the International Space Station, which passes at a different hour each time; these are the passes between 21:00 and 06:00 on clear nights of June to September 2024-2026. Each 60 m cell's value is the median of its cloud-free night views (at least 3; the typical cell has 13), whatever the hour, so a place seen mostly before midnight reads a little warmer than one seen mostly before dawn. A cell belongs to the barrio that holds its centre; a municipio's and Puerto Rico's figures pool the cells of their barrios. Water is left out. The sea stays warm at night, so land near the coast stays warmer too, and elevation cools the land: compare coastal places with each other and the Cordillera with itself.
vars.noValue: Too few cloud-free ECOSTRESS night views
